# S15 / S16 supporting implementation and acceptance review

Status is maintained only in `docs/plugin-module-parity-matrix.md`. This file records the source contract and evidence boundaries, and does not declare global completion.

## Fixed source and retained behavior

Source backend is `jxxghp/MoviePilot@8a83efeacd3e26b82be495e17d50146e31c96a60`. `source-target-bindings.json` records the initial Git blobs/content hashes. Final implementation changes have separate current bindings; historical hashes are retained, not silently relabelled. The frontend remains the existing light-media Vuetify/plugin renderer; no separate browser-control page is introduced.

S15 maps the complete `app/helper/ocr.py:8–75` helper to `internal/app/plugin_original_host_ocr.go` and `internal/plugins/ocr_host.go`. It normalizes the data URL/base64 string, optionally fetches image bytes, posts `base64_img`, preserves the fixed helper's falsey-result behavior, propagates malformed JSON/type failures, and does not turn a non-200 image response into an absent response. Configured image Cookie/UA remain on the host; the separate OCR POST receives neither. A failed image download retains a supplied base64 fallback. The fixed `RequestUtils` dependencies use a temporary Session per request, a 20-second inactivity timeout, 30 redirects, and `gzip, deflate, br` wire support. The five new actual full-source redirect cases demonstrate that configured hostless cookies coexist with same-name scoped redirect cookies, and that a 31-redirect image failure still uses the supplied fallback. The target tests compare the entire observed HTTP trace, not only status 200.

S16 maps `app/helper/browser.py:852–1102`'s required `get_page_source` path to `internal/browserrender/` and the configured-site SDK `sites.render`. It keeps the default headed mode, `goto` then networkidle then document serialization, source default timeout behavior, current UA/Cookie/proxy, FlareSolverr's direct truthy solution semantics, failed/falsey FlareSolverr fallback, authenticated proxy session cleanup, and isolated profile/browser/display cleanup. The pure Go CDP client controls the signed native CloakBrowser binary; it does not use Python or Node at runtime. The production Dockerfile now includes the ordinary native runtime, fonts, shared libraries and Xvfb, instead of only supplying a test image. The same real build exposed and fixed the existing missing frontend build input for `build-icons.mjs` (`COPY internal/plugins /src/internal/plugins`).

`browser-callsite-scope.json` separately records ordinary `action(callback)`: its fixed-core consumer is site auto-login/2FA cookie retrieval (`app/helper/cookie.py:325`, `app/chain/site.py:1369`), outside this plugin-platform migration. It is not classified as AI. All 77 files in the captured installed-plugin snapshot match their recorded hashes, with exactly three required `get_page_source` calls and no `action` call. `_PluginBase` and PluginManager do not expose such callbacks. No callable/session/action framework is added.

## Necessary Go adaptations

- SDK calls use declared methods, configured site handles and JSON values. Site credentials and executable paths stay on the host. Image/page credentials cannot cross origins; configured objects are rechecked when performing I/O. This retains the project's credential and stale-object requirements.
- Message/image/HTML payloads are bounded by the existing SDK limits; errors are safe Go errors/diagnostic codes, without Python traceback or private remote content.
- Source Python wrapper/Playwright is replaced by pure Go CDP plus its native browser. Source's independent native auto-updater becomes a reproducible image build pinned to verified publisher manifests; Go plugin installation/update behavior is unchanged.
- The source requirement `cloakbrowser~=0.5.3` floats within that version series. Existing read-only installation metadata binds wrapper 0.5.6, Playwright 1.62.0 and the publisher's Linux amd64 browser 146.0.7680.177.5 / arm64 146.0.7680.177.3. Both manifests/signatures/digests are recorded in the earlier shared-runtime evidence. Linux acceptance runs on amd64; no ARM hardware execution is claimed.
- Source default headed execution is supported with a per-call Xvfb display. Proxy credentials use a private loopback relay rather than Chromium command arguments. The new actual TLS CONNECT test verifies authentication, valid target TLS, rejection and cleanup.

## Evidence categories and historical failures

`ocr-source/oracle.json` (34 cases) is fixed complete-helper AST execution with synthetic request responses. `ocr-redirect-source-oracle.json` executes the complete fixed helper and selected fixed RequestUtils methods with the actual paired requests/urllib3 dependencies in a new read-only, network-none container and an owned loopback HTTP server. Neither runs the original service or accesses old settings/database data. The target's standard SDK tests install real independently compiled Go workers and use real HTTP/SQLite/process calls. Actual native browser tests execute JavaScript; protocol FlareSolverr/OCR replies remain explicitly owned synthetic service responses and do not prove a public anti-bot challenge or OCR model's recognition accuracy.

The first redirect target test failed on lost redirect cookies and an off-by-one limit (`ocr-redirect-red.log`); it was repaired and the source-bound strict trace tests passed. Product build R1 exposed the missing internal/plugins frontend build input; its original failure remains in `product-image-build-r1.log`. R2 is an intermediate old SDK/OCR context, not final acceptance. Its Linux native run was canceled before a container/test started to serialize Docker graph operations with the final build; `native-linux-r2-not-run.json` records that it was not executed. R3 is the successful full product Dockerfile build, not the final patched Go executable. R4–R6 are explicitly new image digests layered over its exact Debian/native runtime with current Go executables; they are not renamed R3 content. R6 has a separately disclosed late central-source capture (`product-r6-binding-qualification.json`) and cannot represent the new S18 bridge. Final combined acceptance must bind an unchanged before/after compilation input closure.

## Source-matched resource startup and cleanup

Real App execution found a late Chromium profile write after allocator shutdown. `cleanup.go` uses the paired Playwright removal policy (maxRetries10,100ms linear retry delay), retries only transient OS errors, preserves an already acquired HTML document, and joins a cleanup error with the original error so revoked-scope classification survives. A controlled ENOTEMPTY late write to a real owned directory proves the subsequent remove actually deletes the new file; a permanent error and a combined guard/cleanup error remain errors. Original R3 profile residue is preserved as a failed observation.

Paired Playwright1.62.0 uses a180-second browser launch default, independently of30-second goto and the caller's networkidle timeout. The prior chromedp implicit20-second launch failed an actual Chrome wrapper delayed21seconds; the explicit180-second setting passes. Paired PyVirtualDisplay3.0 waits600seconds for displayfd readiness. A real cold App launch hit the prior10-second cap; an actual Xvfb delayed12seconds fails under the old cap and passes after the600-second source adaptation, then its PID is joined. Caller cancellation and early child exit still interrupt. `playwright-launch-timeout-source.json`, `virtual-display-source.json`, the red/green logs and `native-linux-product-r6-normal-final.log` preserve this causal chain.

The R3 test with an extra read-only HOME failed Crashpad startup and is retained as an unsupported extra-environment observation; the user did not require a read-only root filesystem. R5's first delayed-wrapper test used a noexec tmpfs and failed to execute the test wrapper; the diagnostic and normal writable-rootfs rerun are separate. No OS security setting or production container was changed to make either pass.

## Final ordinary proxy behavior

The fixed `config.py:1134–1152` PROXY_SERVER differs from ordinary requests' PROXY: it only uses an explicit PROXY_HOST and preserves literal percent escapes in parsed username/password. The paired0.5.6 wrapper actually returns empty proxy kwargs/args forNone under unset, uppercase and lowercase proxy environments. The host now constructs an internal three-field source dictionary from the explicit existing setting; it does not expose a new plugin credential API or modify ordinary HTTP transports. The actual SDK/owned-FS five-case regression compares source-derived payloads, session sequencing, encoded authentication and the malformed IPv6 server spelling. The old host file is injected with a source-hash-verified Go overlay to demonstrate genuine differential failures; the original shared files are not temporarily rewritten.

The pinned wrapper uses inline native arguments for SOCKS and Linux amd64 HTTP authentication; the paired arm64 free artifact uses Playwright's HTTP proxy options. Actual paired Chromium launcher code only forces loopback through a proxy for the latter options. The Go credential relay now retains those routing modes, including real JS-marked direct/proxy loopback tests. Percent-literal credentials reach an actual verified HTTPS CONNECT proxy unchanged. Password without username retains the source options/authentication mode.

The source IPv6 formatter omitsbrackets. Its FS payload remains literal; actual paired Playwright normalizes that invalid server to the unrelated `http://http`, rather than throwing. The host's configured credential endpoint boundary requires safeNone/`browser_proxy_invalid` without an attempt to that derived host. This is a necessary safety adaptation approved by the coordinator, not a claim that the original native branch raises. The fixed wrapper also passes socks5h literally: executing those exact flags with the pinned native binary produces zero proxy handshakes and ERR_NO_SUPPORTED_PROXIES, with a real SOCKS5 handshake control. The native adapter preservesNone for socks5h; ordinary requests' separate SOCKS5h support remains unchanged.

Existing host settings trim and validate proxy inputs, so the source's schemeless, leading/trailing-space or otherwise invalid settings strings are not independently representable through the current target configuration contract. Those input boundaries are recorded rather than silently imitating a different getter.
